I am 59, farming 40 years, no schooling at all. My mother taught me, and I watched the neighbors. I have 14 mu, just me now, so I hire two young men from the village when I need strong backs for planting and harvest.

I don't change things. Last year I did four mu chili, four mu wheat, two mu cotton, two mu watermelon, two mu garlic. This year the same. If I try something new and it fails, that is a disaster. Better to waste a little fertilizer than to lose yield.

For my chili, four mu, I buy hybrid seedlings from the dealer in town. I put two bags of compound fertilizer on each mu as base — that's 100 jin — then I top-dress twice, half a bag of urea each time. Seven irrigations in summer. Five pesticide sprays, the worms love chili. Last year I got 2500 jin per mu.

Wheat is four mu. Improved seed from the shop, same as my neighbor Lao Zhang. One bag of compound per mu at planting, then one bag of urea when it greens up. Three irrigations. Two sprays. I get about 450 jin per mu.

Cotton two mu. I have always grown cotton. Hybrid seed. One bag compound per mu, half bag urea when it flowers. Four irrigations. Three sprays for bollworm. About 350 jin seed cotton per mu.

Watermelon two mu. Hybrid seeds. Two bags compound per mu, half bag urea when the melons swell. Six irrigations — too much water and they lose sweetness. Three sprays. Good weather, 3500 jin per mu.

Garlic two mu. I plant improved cloves in autumn. One and a half bags compound per mu, half bag urea in spring when it greens up. Four irrigations. Two sprays. About 1200 jin per mu.

I rotary till everything. The machine man charges 30 yuan per mu. I don't plough deep, never saw the point.
